response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, structure, and cross-view consistency for the train state-machine case. Key findings: (1) NL-CONTRACT-REF-002 (DoorsClosing->InMotion on Closed/SendDeparted) is realized only via a compiler-forced macro transition; the working contract shows tr_0003 maps to a protected macro root with a complete member digest and closed target-entry segment, so the endpoint closes through the whole macro rather than one generated segment - satisfied, no candidate. (2) NL-CONTRACT-REF-001 (root->DoorsClosing initial entry) is satisfied by transition:line:38 ([*]->DoorsClosing) - satisfied. However, NL5-INIT-1 (InMotion-local initial entry into Accelerating) is satisfied by transition:line:20 ([*]->Accelerating) - satisfied, omitted. (3) The NL2 transition-group alternatives (InMotion->Stopping vs InMotion->EmergencyStopping) are both realized in FCSTM only through guarded transitions gated by the R45RouteToken variable (set to 8 or 9 by inner-region transitions), not by the literal signals named in NL (Arrived/Stop,Send Arrived and Obstacle Detected respectively) at the InMotion level itself - this is a structural collapse: the outer transitions carry guard-only conditions (R45RouteToken==8/9) with no trigger, while NL requires event-triggered transitions at this exact source/target. This creates wrong-target/mismatched-trigger evidence for NL-CONTRACT-REF-003 and REF-004, but since exact source/target pairs do exist (InMotion->Stopping, InMotion->EmergencyStopping), and events are consumed by inner states via effect-setting transitions, the structural realization is an indirect routing rather than a missing edge. I flag this only where the guard_disjointness contract requires comparison: R45RouteToken==8 and R45RouteToken==9 are mutually exclusive by construagePOV (distinct integer values), so NL-CONTRACT-REF-005 guard_disjointness is actually satisfied - omitted. (4) The containment contracts (REF-008/009/010) are satisfied: Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching are direct children of InMotion per source_inventory and model_ir - satisfied, omitted. (5) NL-CONTRACT-REF-021 (EmergencyStopping contained in InMotion) is a derived contract claiming EmergencyStopping must be a child of InMotion, but source_inventory and FCSTM both show EmergencyStopping as a top-level sibling state, not contained in InMotion - this is a structural containment mismatch worth flagging as a candidate since the NL text ('the system enters the EmergencyStopping state') combined with NL2's placement 'In the InMotion state ... or to the EmergencyStopping state' could be read either as a sibling transition target or as a nested substate; given exact source inventory shows EmergencyStopping as root-level (parent: null), and the working-contract source-to-model trace confirms this as source-owned identity, I evaluate this derived contract as a genuine structural mismatch candidate. (6) The DoorsClosing local initial entry (tr_0002 / transition:line:10) targets a synthetic InvalidInitialtr_0002 placeholder rather than the DoorsClosing state functioning normally - this is compiler-owned per working_contract (compiler:state:...InvalidInitialtr_0002), reflecting a malformed nested initial edge in DoorsClosing's own scope (self-referential PlantUML init that the compiler could not resolve to a real target). This is evidence for NL-CONTRACT-REF-001's owner scope only if DoorsClosing's own initial pseudostate is part of that contract's obligation; but REF-001 concerns root->DoorsClosing entry only, which is satisfied by transition:line:38. The malformed nested DoorsClosing-local initial edge is a separate structural defect not covered by any supplied contract as stated (DoorsClosing has no substates in NL), so it is preserved only as contrastive observation, not a candidate against a contract whose target is satisfied by a different edge.

Key findings: (1) NL-CONTRACT-REF-002 (DoorsClosing->InMotion on Closed/SendDeparted) is realized only via a compiler-forced macro transition; the working contract shows tr_0003 maps to a protected macro root with a complete member digest and closed target-entry segment, so the endpoint closes through the whole macro rather than one generated segment - satisfied, no candidate. (2) NL-CONTRACT-REF-001 (root->DoorsClosing initial entry) is satisfied by transition:line:38 ([*]->DoorsClosing) - satisfied. However, NL5-INIT-1 (InMotion-local initial entry into Accelerating) is satisfied by transition:line:20 ([*]->Accelerating) - satisfied, omitted. (3) The NL2 transition-group alternatives (InMotion->Stopping vs InMotion->EmergencyStopping) are both realized in FCSTM only through guarded transitions gated by the R45RouteToken variable (set to 8 or 9 by inner-region transitions), not by the literal signals named in NL (Arrived/Stop,Send Arrived and Obstacle Detected respectively) at the InMotion level itself - this is a structural collapse: the outer transitions carry guard-only conditions (R45RouteToken==8/9) with no trigger, while NL requires event-triggered transitions at this exact source/target. This creates wrong-target/mismatched-trigger evidence for NL-CONTRACT-REF-003 and REF-004, but since exact source/target pairs do exist (InMotion->Stopping, InMotion->EmergencyStopping), and events are consumed by inner states via effect-setting transitions, the structural realization is an indirect routing rather than a missing edge. I flag this only where the guard_disjointness contract requires comparison: R45RouteToken==8 and R45RouteToken==9 are mutually exclusive by construagePOV (distinct integer values), so NL-CONTRACT-REF-005 guard_disjointness is actually satisfied - omitted. (4) The containment contracts (REF-008/009/010) are satisfied: Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching are direct children of InMotion per source_inventory and model_ir - satisfied, omitted. (5) NL-CONTRACT-REF-021 (EmergencyStopping contained in InMotion) is a derived contract claiming EmergencyStopping must be a child of InMotion, but source_inventory and FCSTM both show EmergencyStopping as a top-level sibling state, not contained in InMotion - this is a structural containment mismatch worth flagging as a candidate since the NL text ('the system enters the EmergencyStopping state') combined with NL2's placement 'In the InMotion state ... or to the EmergencyStopping state' could be read either as a sibling transition target or as a nested substate; given exact source inventory shows EmergencyStopping as root-level (parent: null), and the working-contract source-to-model trace confirms this as source-owned identity, I evaluate this derived contract as a genuine structural mismatch candidate. (6) The DoorsClosing local initial entry (tr_0002 / transition:line:10) targets a synthetic InvalidInitialtr_0002 placeholder rather than the DoorsClosing state functioning normally - this is compiler-owned per working_contract (compiler:state:...InvalidInitialtr_0002), reflecting a malformed nested initial edge in DoorsClosing's own scope (self-referential PlantUML init that the compiler could not resolve to a real target). This is evidence for NL-CONTRACT-REF-001's owner scope only if DoorsClosing's own initial pseudostate is part of that contract's obligation; but REF-001 concerns root->DoorsClosing entry only, which is satisfied by transition:line:38. The malformed nested DoorsClosing-local initial edge is a separate structural defect not covered by any supplied contract as stated (DoorsClosing has no substates in NL), so it is preserved only as contrastive observation, not a candidate against a contract whose target is satisfied by a different edge.

Key findings: (1) InMotion->Stopping and InMotion->EmergencyStopping are guarded internal transitions gated by R45RouteToken, which is set only by inner Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching->[*] segments triggered by Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived/Obstacle_Detected; these are complete and reachable, satisfying NL2 endpoint contracts operationally. (2) EmergencyStopping and Stopping are both LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING reachable states (deterministic diagnostics), making the terminal-scope-exit obligation for EmergencyStopping's send-signal effect operationally consequential but not itself a termination defect since NL does not designate either as a formal completion/termination_state role (state_role is operating_state or null, not termination_state) -- so no termination candidate is warranted per contract typing. (3) The InMotion->EmergencyStopping guarded transition exists and is reachable, and Obstacle_Detected is declared and reachably consumed inside InMotion (by the inner Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching->[*] segments), so the NL2-DERIVED event-consumer-coverage contract is satisfied at the InMotion scope: the obstacle-detected condition is consumed by reachable inner transitions that route into the guarded outer edge. (4) The nested initial edge DoorsClosing->[*]->InvalidInitialtr_0002 is a synthetic placeholder scoped to DoorsClosing (NL1-INIT-1 owner=root/system, target=DoorsClosing); the actual required root->DoorsClosing edge is present and satisfied, so no candidate for NL1-INIT-1. However, the malformed nested DoorsClosing-owned initial edge to a synthetic invalid target is a distinct owner-local defect not covered by any supplied contract at that exact owner scope (DoorsClosing owns its own child initial edge), and per protocol this is preserved as supporting evidence only, not an independent candidate absent a supplied contract naming that owner scope.
